name: Mutton Karahi
description: Tender mutton cooked in a concentrated tomato karahi masala with ginger, green chilies and freshly ground spices.
ingredients: ½–1 cup hot water, only as needed
method: Heat oil in a karahi or heavy pan over medium-high heat. Add the mutton and fry for 6–8 minutes until it changes colour and begins to brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook briefly, then add tomatoes and salt. Cook until the tomatoes soften and begin forming a thick masala.
Add a small amount of hot water, cover and cook over medium-low heat until the mutton is tender. Add more hot water only if needed during cooking.
Uncover once the meat is tender and cook over medium-high heat, stirring frequently, until excess moisture evaporates and the masala clings to the meat.
Add crushed cumin, black pepper and green chilies. Cook for another 3–5 minutes until the oil begins to separate at the edges.
Taste for salt, garnish generously with fresh ginger and serve hot with naan or roti.
tips: Mutton may need longer than 70 minutes depending on the cut and age of the meat; tenderness is more important than a fixed clock time.
Avoid adding a large amount of water at once because karahi should finish with a concentrated tomato masala rather than a thin gravy.
storage: Cool promptly and refrigerate covered for up to 2 days. Reheat until piping hot throughout.
